candidates.working_title: Permission to Be Here Is Not Permission to Do That
candidates.core_evergreen_question: How does a foreigner tell the difference between the right to remain in Indonesia and the right to perform a specific activity while there?
candidates.target_audience: Newly arrived foreigners, visitors drifting toward residency, remote workers, and anyone who was told their permit 'covers everything'
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The relief of an approved permit collides with the quiet dread of being asked, by an official or a competitor, what exactly you are allowed to do with it.
candidates.why_intriguing: Almost every foreigner conflates stay rights with activity rights, and the conflation is invisible until someone tests it — usually at the worst possible moment.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Every immigration system separates duration of stay from permitted activity as a structural matter; only the permit names, portals, and categories change.
candidates.narrative_promise: A two-question test — what am I permitted to do, and who decided that — that can be applied to any permit, in any year, before acting on it.

candidates.working_title: Your Status Belongs to Someone Else
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What happens to a foreigner's legal position when the sponsor or guarantor holding their status stops being aligned with their interests?
candidates.target_audience: Employees, foreign spouses, dependents, and investors whose stay depends on a company or individual guarantor
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The person or entity that makes your life in Indonesia possible is also the one who can end it, and the relationship is rarely negotiated with that in mind.
candidates.why_intriguing: People negotiate salary, equity, and rent aggressively, then accept sponsorship terms without reading them — the one agreement that governs whether they can stay at all.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Sponsorship and guarantor structures are foundational to how permits are issued to non-citizens; the dependency survives any renaming of the permit.
candidates.narrative_promise: What to agree with a sponsor while everyone is still friendly, and the early signals that a sponsor relationship is quietly becoming leverage.

candidates.working_title: The Agent Who Knows More About Your Status Than You Do
candidates.core_evergreen_question: How much of your own immigration file should you personally understand, hold, and be able to reproduce without your agent?
candidates.target_audience: Foreigners who delegate permits, extensions, and reporting to intermediaries and never see the underlying documents
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Convenience purchased with trust, plus the embarrassment of asking questions that would reveal you never understood your own case.
candidates.why_intriguing: The failure mode is silence: nothing looks wrong until a renewal is refused, and by then the person who could explain it has stopped answering.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Intermediaries will always exist where procedures are complex, foreign-language, and relationship-driven; the dependency outlives any specific process reform.
candidates.narrative_promise: The minimum personal file every foreigner should be able to produce on demand, and the questions that separate a competent agent from an expensive one.

candidates.working_title: 'Everyone Does It' Is Not a Legal Category
candidates.core_evergreen_question: How should a foreigner weigh visible common practice against the written rule and the discretion of whoever enforces it?
candidates.target_audience: Long-stayers, small operators, and members of expat communities who calibrate risk by watching each other
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Social proof feels like safety, but enforcement lands on individuals — and the person who gets checked is always alone.
candidates.why_intriguing: It names the exact cognitive shortcut most foreigners run on, and shows why a crowd is a terrible source of legal advice.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The gap between tolerated practice and formal rule is permanent in every jurisdiction; only the specific tolerated practices rotate.
candidates.narrative_promise: A way to price the risk of a common practice — exposure, reversibility, who bears it — instead of simply copying the person next to you.

candidates.working_title: Small Status Errors Do Not Stay Small
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Why do minor immigration lapses compound instead of fading, and at what point does a cheap problem become a permanent one?
candidates.target_audience: Anyone living on temporary status, families managing multiple permits, and frequent travelers
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Procrastination meets a system that counts, records, and remembers — and the discovery usually happens at a counter, not at a desk where it could be fixed.
candidates.why_intriguing: It reframes immigration as an information problem you can close in advance rather than a bureaucratic ambush you endure.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Time-based obligations and permanent records are structural to immigration control; the counting continues regardless of which system does it.
candidates.narrative_promise: The earliest detection points and a personal pre-travel audit that surfaces a status problem before an official does.

candidates.working_title: When the Relationship Changes, So Does the Permit
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What happens to residency built on a family relationship when that relationship ends, changes, or is questioned?
candidates.target_audience: Foreign spouses, mixed-nationality families, dependent children, and partners considering marriage in Indonesia
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Legal status entangled with love: asking the practical questions feels like an accusation, so nobody asks until it is an emergency.
candidates.why_intriguing: It is the most emotionally loaded category in immigration and the least discussed, because raising it sounds like planning to fail.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Derived and dependent status is a permanent architecture in immigration law; the human consequences of dependency do not change with the form number.
candidates.narrative_promise: What each partner should understand and hold independently while things are good, and how derived status can be made less fragile.

candidates.working_title: Where Does Your Work Actually Happen?
candidates.core_evergreen_question: For someone living in Indonesia while earning from abroad, which country's rules attach to the work — and why is the answer not simply 'the one that pays me'?
candidates.target_audience: Remote employees, freelancers, agency owners, and self-described digital nomads on long stays
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The self-image of a visitor who happens to open a laptop, versus systems that measure physical presence and where value is actually created.
candidates.why_intriguing: Two different systems — immigration and tax — answer the same question with different logic, and most people assume one answer covers both.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Cross-border remote work is structurally permanent, and the presence-versus-payment question predates and will outlast any nomad-specific permit.
candidates.narrative_promise: Separate the three questions people mash into one — may I stay, may I do this, and who may tax it — and answer them in the right order.

candidates.working_title: What Your Residency Permit Does Not Come With
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Which rights do foreigners wrongly assume are bundled into a residency status, and which must be obtained separately?
candidates.target_audience: New residents, retirees, investors, and anyone who believes a long-stay permit unlocks property, banking, work, and tax outcomes automatically
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The permit arrives and feels like citizenship-lite; the discovery that it is a narrow key, not a master key, comes later and usually mid-transaction.
candidates.why_intriguing: It maps a specific and very common false mental model — the bundle fallacy — rather than reciting one rule.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Immigration status, commercial rights, property rights, and tax status are governed by separate regimes everywhere; the unbundling is permanent.
candidates.narrative_promise: A clean separation of what residency grants, what it merely enables, and what it has nothing to do with.

candidates.working_title: The Agreement That Cannot Be Enforced
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What is a private side agreement actually worth when it contradicts what the public record says about ownership?
candidates.target_audience: Foreign investors, would-be owners using local names, and anyone reassured that 'the lawyer wrote it, so it is protected'
candidates.recurring_human_tension: You paid for something you can only defend by revealing the arrangement that may make it unenforceable — the trap is self-sealing.
candidates.why_intriguing: It explains why the strongest-looking document folder can be the weakest position, and why the paperwork often exists to comfort the buyer rather than protect them.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The structural conflict between a public register and a contradicting private promise is permanent in any system with registered ownership.
candidates.narrative_promise: A stress test for any structure: name the bad day, then trace who would have to do what, in front of whom, for you to recover.

candidates.working_title: Who Can Actually Stop You?
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Which roles in an Indonesian company hold which powers, and how does a foreign founder end up with the title but not the control?
candidates.target_audience: Foreign founders, joint-venture partners, minority investors, and anyone accepting a corporate role they did not choose
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Relief at a structure that looks clean on the certificate, followed by the discovery of a veto, signature, or approval you handed away without noticing.
candidates.why_intriguing: It maps power rather than paperwork — who can block a bank transfer, a licence change, or your own removal.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The separation of ownership, management, and supervision is a durable feature of company law; the titles persist even as procedures digitize.
candidates.narrative_promise: A control map to draw before signing: for each critical action, who can do it, who can block it, and who can undo it.

candidates.working_title: Your Licence Describes a Business You May Not Be Running
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What happens over time when a company's registered scope of activity drifts away from what it actually does day to day?
candidates.target_audience: Founders who pivoted, operators who added revenue lines, and anyone whose business grew faster than its paperwork
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Growth feels like success and looks like drift; nobody wants to reopen a licensing file that took months to close.
candidates.why_intriguing: It reframes business classification as an identity the state holds about you, not a formality you completed once at incorporation.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Activity classification and scope-based licensing are a permanent architecture even as codes, portals, and risk tiers are reorganized.
candidates.narrative_promise: An annual review — does our registered identity still describe us — and the signals that a pivot has outgrown its licence.

candidates.working_title: A Company You Stopped Using Is Still Alive
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What continues to be owed by a company with no revenue, and how do people accumulate liability simply by walking away?
candidates.target_audience: Founders whose venture paused or failed, holders of legacy entities, and anyone who 'stopped using' a structure without closing it
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The wish that abandonment equals closure, meeting a legal person that keeps existing, keeps reporting, and keeps accruing.
candidates.why_intriguing: Silent accrual is the least dramatic and most expensive failure mode — nothing happens for years, then everything does.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Entities exist until formally dissolved in every corporate system; the distinction between inactive and closed is structural.
candidates.narrative_promise: The difference between dormant, deregistered, and dissolved — and what each actually requires of the owner.

candidates.working_title: Where the Corporate Shield Leaks
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Under what circumstances does a foreign director or shareholder become personally exposed despite operating through a limited-liability company?
candidates.target_audience: Directors, founders, signatories, and foreigners accepting a corporate position as a favor or a formality
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The comfort of a legal form versus the ordinary acts — a signature, a payment, a filing not made — that quietly pierce it.
candidates.why_intriguing: Most people learn the phrase 'limited liability' and stop there; the interesting content is the list of exceptions nobody mentions at incorporation.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Director duties and the limits of the corporate veil are foundational concepts, not policy of the moment.
candidates.narrative_promise: The categories of personal exposure to check before accepting a directorship, and the habits that keep the shield intact.

candidates.working_title: Whoever Holds the Logins Holds the Company
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Who really controls a company when licensing, tax, and banking access sits in someone else's hands?
candidates.target_audience: Foreign owners relying on local staff, accountants, or agents to operate official systems on their behalf
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Administrative convenience hardening into dependency, and the discomfort of asking for credentials from someone you have trusted for years.
candidates.why_intriguing: It shows that control is practical as well as legal — you can own a company on paper and still be locked out of it in practice.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Official processes will keep moving onto credentialed systems; whoever holds authentication will keep holding operational leverage.
candidates.narrative_promise: A credential-custody checklist: what an owner should always hold, what can be delegated, and how to test access before you need it.

candidates.working_title: You Are Also Buying Its Past
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What does a buyer inherit when acquiring an existing Indonesian company instead of forming a new one?
candidates.target_audience: Acquirers, buyers of 'ready-made' or shelf entities, and founders tempted by a shortcut to being operational
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Speed and impatience meeting an unknown history, sold with a smile by someone who knows exactly what is in it.
candidates.why_intriguing: The attraction — it already exists, it is already licensed — is precisely the source of the risk.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Successor liability and the inheritance of an entity's history are structural features of buying a legal person rather than starting one.
candidates.narrative_promise: The buried-liability checklist, and what to insist on seeing before the shares move rather than after.

candidates.working_title: The Handshake Hire Becomes a Legal Relationship
candidates.core_evergreen_question: At what point does an informal working arrangement with local staff become a formal employment obligation, regardless of what was verbally agreed?
candidates.target_audience: Small operators, villa and hospitality owners, agency founders, and foreigners who employ people they consider friends or family
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Generosity and personal loyalty on one side, accruing entitlements that do not switch off on the other — and the pain of a dispute with someone you like.
candidates.why_intriguing: It exposes how informality is a one-way door: easy to enter, and interpreted against the employer on the way out.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Labor protection based on the substance of a relationship rather than its label is a durable principle across jurisdictions.
candidates.narrative_promise: How informality converts into obligation, what to document from day one, and how to end an arrangement without turning it into a claim.

candidates.working_title: Your Passport Does Not Decide Where You Pay Tax
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What actually determines whether someone becomes an Indonesian tax resident, and why is it disconnected from nationality and visa type?
candidates.target_audience: Long-stayers, remote workers, retirees, and people who split the year across countries
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Self-image — 'I don't really live here' — versus the objective way presence and life-center are measured by someone else.
candidates.why_intriguing: People believe they choose their tax residence; the durable insight is that it is largely determined by facts they create without noticing.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Residence tests based on presence and center of life are the international norm; thresholds may move, the logic does not.
candidates.narrative_promise: The questions a tax authority actually asks, translated into a self-assessment you can run before anyone asks them.

candidates.working_title: 'I Already Paid Tax at Home'
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Why does having paid tax in another country not automatically prevent a claim in Indonesia, and what must a person do to turn a treaty into actual relief?
candidates.target_audience: Dual-country earners, employees of foreign companies, and owners of income-producing assets abroad
candidates.recurring_human_tension: A powerful fairness instinct — I already paid, this is double — running into relief that exists only as a procedure someone has to perform.
candidates.why_intriguing: It converts a vague comfort ('there's a treaty') into a concrete chain of documents, and shows where that chain usually breaks.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Treaty relief has always been claim-based and evidence-based; the specific certificates and forms change, the mechanism does not.
candidates.narrative_promise: The paperwork chain that turns a treaty from a reassuring idea into a reduction you can actually defend.

candidates.working_title: Profitable and Broke
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Why do foreign-owned businesses in Indonesia run out of cash while showing a profit, and how do withholding and payment timing create the gap?
candidates.target_audience: Founders and operators of small and mid-sized businesses, especially service and hospitality
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The spreadsheet says yes and the bank account says no, and the owner assumes it is a bookkeeping mistake rather than structure.
candidates.why_intriguing: It connects an abstract compliance topic to the most visceral business experience there is — not being able to pay people this month.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Withholding, prepayment, and timing mismatches between recognition and cash are permanent features of tax systems.
candidates.narrative_promise: A timing map of when money leaves before it arrives, and the reserve discipline that keeps a profitable business alive.

candidates.working_title: One Wallet, Two Lives
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What goes wrong, legally and practically, when a foreign owner treats company money as personal money?
candidates.target_audience: Sole operators, family businesses, and founders who fund the company from their own pocket and take from it the same way
candidates.recurring_human_tension: 'It's my company, so it's my money' is emotionally true and structurally false, and the belief survives until an audit, a partner, or a buyer tests it.
candidates.why_intriguing: It is the single most common financial failure mode among foreign small operators, and it is invisible while things are going well.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The separation between a legal person's assets and its owner's is foundational; enforcement tools evolve, the principle does not.
candidates.narrative_promise: The separation habits that hold up under scrutiny, and how to unwind years of mixing without making it worse.

candidates.working_title: How Do You Stop Being a Taxpayer Here?
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What does it actually take to end tax obligations in Indonesia, and what happens to people who simply leave?
candidates.target_audience: Departing residents, founders closing a business, and anyone treating relocation as a clean break
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The fantasy of walking away versus the fear of what waits if you ever come back — a fear people manage by not looking.
candidates.why_intriguing: Everyone plans the entry into a system and almost nobody plans the exit, which is where the unpleasant surprises accumulate.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Deregistration as a documented process, rather than an event that happens automatically on departure, is a durable design in tax administration.
candidates.narrative_promise: Exit treated as a process with a paper trail — what to close, in what order, and what evidence to keep afterwards.

candidates.working_title: Someone Files in Your Name
candidates.core_evergreen_question: When a third party handles your filings and payments, what should you always be able to see, verify, and keep?
candidates.target_audience: Foreigners and business owners using accountants, agents, or office staff for compliance they never review
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Trust combined with opacity, plus the private shame of not understanding a return that carries your name and your responsibility.
candidates.why_intriguing: The person who signs is not always the person who answers for it, and most people never learn which one they are.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Delegated compliance with retained personal responsibility is a permanent arrangement wherever procedures are technical and local.
candidates.narrative_promise: Three artifacts to demand every cycle, and how to confirm that a payment reached the state rather than an intermediary.

candidates.working_title: The Assumption That Nobody Is Looking
candidates.core_evergreen_question: How should a foreigner plan when they cannot know what the authorities can already see about their money, property, and movements?
candidates.target_audience: Cross-border earners, property owners, and anyone whose informal structure depends on remaining unnoticed
candidates.recurring_human_tension: A strategy built on invisibility ages badly, but abandoning it means admitting the past years were exposure rather than cleverness.
candidates.why_intriguing: It shifts the question from 'will they find out' to 'what would I do if they already had' — a far more useful and uncomfortable frame.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Data-matching and cross-border information sharing have moved in one direction for decades; the trend outlasts any specific mechanism.
candidates.narrative_promise: How to build a position that survives visibility, and how to think about correcting a past that assumed the opposite.

candidates.working_title: You Did Not Buy the Land, You Bought a Clock
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What does a foreigner actually acquire when they 'buy' property in Indonesia — which right, held by whom, and for how long?
candidates.target_audience: Villa buyers, retirees, lifestyle investors, and anyone told they can own property here in the ordinary sense of the word
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The emotional weight of the word 'ownership' against the specific, time-limited instrument actually in hand.
candidates.why_intriguing: It replaces the most consequential misunderstanding in the market with three concrete questions anyone can ask in a first meeting.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Tiered land rights with different holders, durations, and transferability are a permanent structure of Indonesian land law.
candidates.narrative_promise: Translate any offer, brochure, or verbal promise into the right, the holder, and the end date — before emotion sets the price.

candidates.working_title: A Promise to Extend Is Not a Right to Extend
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What is a future renewal worth when it depends on the consent of someone whose leverage grows as your term shortens?
candidates.target_audience: Leaseholders, long-term tenants, business operators on rented land, and buyers of rights with years already used
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Optimism at signing, when everyone is agreeable, versus the imbalance at renewal, when you have built something you cannot move.
candidates.why_intriguing: It exposes an option most people treat as a certainty, and shows that the negotiating position was set years earlier.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The difference between a contractual right and a discretionary consent is a permanent legal distinction, independent of term lengths.
candidates.narrative_promise: How to convert a promise into something enforceable — or, failing that, how to price the uncertainty honestly and plan the exit.

candidates.working_title: Check the Seller, Not Just the Land
candidates.core_evergreen_question: How do you verify that the person offering land is actually entitled to offer it, and who else might hold a claim?
candidates.target_audience: Buyers, lessees, developers, and anyone negotiating with a confident intermediary rather than a documented owner
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Charm, confidence, and community standing substituting for entitlement — and the awkwardness of asking a friendly person to prove who they are.
candidates.why_intriguing: The most expensive property failures are rarely about the land itself; they are about heirs, co-owners, and authority that was never checked.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Family, inheritance, and communal claims over land are a durable social reality that no registry reform fully erases.
candidates.narrative_promise: The entitlement chain to trace before money moves, and the specific people who should be in the room when it does.

candidates.working_title: Legal Land, Illegal Plan
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Why can perfectly valid land still be unable to host the building or business you intend, and when should you discover that?
candidates.target_audience: Buyers planning villas, restaurants, retreats, and rental operations on land they have already fallen in love with
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Commitment to a location precedes verification of what it permits, and by the time the answer arrives, retreat feels like failure.
candidates.why_intriguing: It separates two questions people fuse into one — can I hold this land, and can I do my thing on it — with very different answers.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Spatial planning and use-based restrictions are permanent instruments of land governance, however the zones are drawn or renamed.
candidates.narrative_promise: A sequence that puts use-verification before deposit, and the questions to ask about a plot's intended purpose rather than its view.

candidates.working_title: You Inherit the Building's Sins
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What does a buyer take on when acquiring a structure whose permits were never obtained, or never matched what was actually built?
candidates.target_audience: Buyers of finished villas, existing businesses, and turnkey properties marketed as 'ready to operate'
candidates.recurring_human_tension: A beautiful completed building feels like proof that everything was done correctly, when it is evidence of nothing at all.
candidates.why_intriguing: It attacks a visual heuristic — it exists, therefore it was allowed — that is almost universally trusted and frequently wrong.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The gap between what is built and what was permitted, and the way that gap transfers to buyers, is a durable structural risk.
candidates.narrative_promise: How to test whether what stands was ever allowed to stand, and what a mismatch costs the person holding it at the wrong moment.

candidates.working_title: Who Will Buy It From You?
candidates.core_evergreen_question: Before acquiring a right in Indonesian property, how do you assess whether and how you can convert it back into money?
candidates.target_audience: Investors treating property as savings, buyers of shortening rights, and anyone planning to leave eventually
candidates.recurring_human_tension: Entry is crowded, celebratory, and well-advised; exit is quiet, lonely, and improvised years later under time pressure.
candidates.why_intriguing: It asks the last question first, and reveals that liquidity — not legality — is what determines whether the investment worked.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: Transferability, buyer pools, and the decay of time-limited rights are structural realities independent of market cycles.
candidates.narrative_promise: An exit test to run before entry: who the future buyer is, what they will be buying, and what will be left of it by then.

candidates.working_title: The Notary Is Not Your Lawyer
candidates.core_evergreen_question: What is the actual role of the official who formalizes your transaction, and what are they not responsible for on your behalf?
candidates.target_audience: Property buyers, lessees, company founders, and anyone who felt reassured simply because a deed was signed before an official
candidates.recurring_human_tension: The deep human need for an authority figure to have checked things, meeting a role that certifies form rather than protecting your interests.
candidates.why_intriguing: It examines a misunderstood relationship at the exact moment people feel safest — the signing — and explains why that feeling is misplaced.
candidates.why_still_relevant_in_three_years: The distinction between an official who authenticates a transaction and an advisor who represents a party is a durable feature of civil-law systems.
candidates.narrative_promise: What to ask before a signing, which protections nobody in the room is providing, and who you would actually need to hire for them.
